jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Louisiana, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Louisiana, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — parish, Louisiana Senate, Louisiana House and U.S. House districts, police jury and parish council districts, cities, towns and villages, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: Louisiana district map, what district am I in, Louisiana Senate district, Louisiana House district, Louisiana congressional district, Louisiana police jury, Louisiana parish council, Louisiana school district lookup

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 6 congressional districts — the largest districts Louisiana carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 4 (119th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 6 features for Louisiana, measured 2026-10-20. LAYER 4 AND NOT LAYER 0: layer 0 already carries the map of Act 2 of the 2026 regular session, which nobody has been elected from yet, while the six members in office were elected in 2024 from the map of Act 2 of the 2024 First Extraordinary Session and serve until noon on 3 January 2027. Measured against the legislature's own file of that 2024 plan, layer 4 matches every district, while layer 0 would put about a quarter of the state in a differently numbered district. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Louisiana Senate District
layers.rank_note: 39 Senate districts — larger on average than a parish, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Louisiana Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 39 features, measured 2026-10-20. These are the plan of the 2022 First Extraordinary Session, which the sitting senators were elected from in 2023. Act 955 of the 2026 regular session moves precincts between Senate Districts 33, 34 and 35 from the next election, in 2027, and keeps the sitting senators' terms, so those new lines are not drawn yet. The Census's feature for the open water of Lake Pontchartrain, which it assigns to no Senate district, is left out. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: la-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Louisiana Senate's own list of senators and each senator's own page: the name as the senator's page writes it, the party, the district office's address and telephone, and the e-mail address the list prints. The list shows a vacant seat as a card reading Vacant, and the card says so: Senate District 14 on 2026-10-20. The pages also name a legislative assistant and a fax number, and neither is read.
source.applies: Louisiana — statewide, all 39 districts. A point on the open water of Lake Pontchartrain is in no Senate district on the Census's map, and the card says so.

layers.label: Parish
layers.rank_note: 64 parishes, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which parish contains the point, and the members of its police jury, council or commission, with its parish president or mayor where the parish elects one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 64 features, measured 2026-10-20. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: la-parish-officials.json, rebuilt weekly: every member of each parish's governing body — 38 police juries, 25 parish councils and Caddo's parish commission — by district, the at-large members of the seven councils that elect some, and the parish president, mayor-president or mayor of the 25 council parishes, from the Louisiana Secretary of State's list of elected officials (573 members on 2026-10-20). An official's own telephone ships where the list prints it for that official alone. A telephone printed for three or more of a body's members is the body's office telephone, and an address ships only as a body's office, where at least three members print the same one, because some officials' addresses are homes. The list also records each official's race and gender, and neither is read.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 69 school districts covering the whole state, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 69 features for Louisiana, measured 2026-10-20.

source.people: la-school-board-members.json, rebuilt weekly from the Louisiana Secretary of State's list of elected officials: every member of the 69 school boards by seat, the 64 parish boards and the five city systems' (Baker, Bogalusa, Central, Monroe and Zachary), 639 members on 2026-10-20. A member's own telephone ships where the list prints it for that member alone, and an address only as the board's office, where at least three of its members print the same one and no official outside the board does. The map does not draw school board districts, so the card lists the whole board and does not say which member represents the point (gap la-school-board-district-lines). 610 of the 639 terms end on December 31, 2026. The list also records each member's race and gender, and neither is read.
source.applies: Louisiana — statewide. The label carries no qualifier because there is nothing to distinguish it from: the elementary and secondary tilings TIGERweb serves for other states are EMPTY in Louisiana (0 features each, measured 2026-10-20), and the 69 unified districts' Census land area sums to exactly the 64-parish total (111,943 km2).

layers.label: Louisiana House District
layers.rank_note: 105 House districts — smaller on average than a school district, larger than a ZIP code

source.answers: The Louisiana House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 105 features, measured 2026-10-20. These are the plan of the 2022 First Extraordinary Session, which the sitting representatives were elected from in 2023. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: la-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Louisiana House's own list of representatives and each representative's own page, on the same terms as the Senate roster; House Districts 77 and 92 read vacant on 2026-10-20.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 540 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas overlapping Louisiana, of the 831 in the state's own bounding box, in a mirrored tile archive (measured 2026-10-21); about 194 km2 of land on average for the 540 and 244 km2 for the 831, and ranked by the 831, which are what the map draws where the archive is not used (on the raster basemap); the layer hides outside Louisiana

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='22'. 831 features in Louisiana's box, measured 2026-10-20.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Louisiana. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (Orange, Texas gives 77630 and Vicksburg, Mississippi 39183, measured 2026-10-20).

layers.label: Police Jury or Council District
layers.rank_note: 56 districts in the 6 parishes whose current lines are confirmed, about 212 km2 of land on average against 244 km2 for a ZIP code in the state's bounding box; drawn only in those parishes

source.answers: Which member of the parish's police jury, council or commission represents the point, in the parishes where this app has confirmed the current district lines. The layer is hidden in the other parishes, where the Parish card still names every member.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — tigerWMS_Current, layer 22 (County Subdivisions, January 1, 2026 vintage), where the Census files each parish's governing-body districts as nonfunctioning county subdivisions; pre-built and shipped with the app for the 6 parishes whose lines the Census changed after the 2020 census and whose districts hold nearly equal numbers of people on that census's own blocks (6.0% to 9.2% apart, measured 2026-10-20): Assumption, Caddo, Lafourche, St. Charles, Tangipahoa and Terrebonne. Elsewhere the Census still carries older lines, which are not drawn.

source.people: la-parish-officials.json, the roster the Parish card reads: the member elected from each district, from the Louisiana Secretary of State's list of elected officials, joined by district number.
source.applies: 6 of Louisiana's 64 parishes; hidden in the other 58, which the Data gaps panel lists and explains.

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 3,569 precincts tiling the state, pre-built from the Louisiana Legislature's statewide precinct file — 37.70 km2 mean area, land and water (median 4.65), measured 2026-10-21 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a police jury or council district (about 212 km2 of land), larger than a city, town or village (about 16 km2 of land)

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point — where a reader votes and how their ballots are reported.

boundary.label: Louisiana Legislature, redistricting office — 2026 Precinct Shapefiles (01-27-2026), one zipped shapefile of every precinct in all 64 parishes, listed on the office's precinct shapefiles page; 3,569 precincts, pre-built for the state by la/scripts/build_la_precincts.py and shipped with the app (Douglas-Peucker at 12 m). The file's five areas of Lake Pontchartrain that it marks as in no voting district, one in each lake parish and with no one living in them, are left out.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody — it is an election-administration unit, not a district with a representative — so the card says that rather than leaving a reader to wonder which name is absent.

layers.label: City, Town or Village
layers.rank_note: 305 incorporated places, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The city, town or village containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 305 features for Louisiana (71 cities, 127 towns and 107 villages), measured 2026-10-20. The Census records two of the cities, Baton Rouge and Lafayette, as partly consolidated with another government, and one, Houma, as having no government of its own, and the card says so.

source.people: la-municipal-officials.json, rebuilt weekly from the Louisiana Secretary of State's list of elected officials: the mayor, the council members, aldermen, selectmen or trustees (the list's own words) by seat where the list gives one, and the chief of police, marshal or city prosecutor, of 302 municipalities on 2026-10-20 (298 mayors, 1,308 members and 191 police officers). Every place the Census draws has a record except New Orleans, whose mayor and council the Parish card names as Orleans Parish's government, Baton Rouge, whose government is East Baton Rouge Parish's, and Houma, which has none of its own. An official's own telephone ships where the list prints it for that official alone, and an address only as the town's office, where at least three of its officials print the same one and no official outside the town does. The map does not draw any town's wards or districts, so the card does not say which member represents the point (gap la-municipal-ward-lines). The list also records each official's race and gender, and neither is read.
source.applies: Louisiana — statewide. A point outside every city, town and village is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — Louisiana has 6 pieces held by four nations, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py on 2026-10-20: the Chitimacha Reservation (1.820 km², St. Mary Parish); the Coushatta Reservation (2.761 km² in 5 parts, Allen Parish) and the Coushatta Off-Reservation Trust Land (8.592 km² in 9 parts, 7.816 km² of it in Allen Parish and the rest in Natchitoches, Calcasieu and Jefferson Davis); the Jena Band of Choctaw Reservation (1.763 km² in 6 parts, Grant and LaSalle parishes); and the Tunica-Biloxi Reservation (1.690 km²) and Off-Reservation Trust Land (4.412 km² in 5 parts), both in Avoyelles Parish. About 3.5 km² a piece on average against about 16 km² for a city, town or village (4,826 km² across 305 places), so ranked after municipalities and before the point layers, as Mississippi's is, and drawn above the larger areas around it. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — Louisiana has 6 such areas, held by the Chitimacha Tribe of Louisiana, the Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana, the Jena Band of Choctaw Indians and the Tunica-Biloxi Indian Tribe.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: Each nation's council from that nation's own page, read weekly by scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py and dated on the card: the Chitimacha Tribal Council's five members (chitimacha.gov), the Jena Band's Tribal Chief and four council members (jenachoctaw.org) and the Tunica-Biloxi Tribal Council's seven members (tunicabiloxi.org). The Coushatta Tribe's own site names its chairman and not the other four members, so its card names nobody and says why. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json); the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Louisiana — the six pieces of land above, in Allen, Avoyelles, Calcasieu, Grant, Jefferson Davis, LaSalle, Natchitoches and St. Mary parishes. Every other point in the state is on no tribal land the Census draws for a government.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-20: 522 points in Louisiana's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Louisiana — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: New Orleans City Hall, 1300 Perdido Street, Orleans Parish

negative_point.note: open water about 50 km south of the Louisiana coast, past the state's offshore line — outside Louisiana and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-20: TIGERweb's state and county layers name no state or parish here, its legislative layers no district, and its ZIP layer no ZIP code (control: New Orleans City Hall returns Louisiana, Orleans Parish and 70112). OPEN WATER BECAUSE A POINT ON A NEIGHBOUR'S LAND WOULD HAVE TO MOVE: Arkansas and Mississippi are live already, and the fleet is meant to reach every state, Texas included.

geometry.note: The whole-Louisiana outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the 64-parish fabric.
The 64 parishes — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 6 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 4 (CD119), until 3 January 2027.
The police jury, council and commission districts of the 6 parishes whose current lines are confirmed (la/scripts/build_la_parish_districts.py).

Every Louisiana voting precinct, pre-built by la/scripts/build_la_precincts.py through scripts/statewide_precincts.py from the Legislature's statewide precinct file, its edition of 27 January 2026 (Douglas-Peucker at 12 m, the smallest of 4, 8 and 12 m that keeps the file at or under 2.5 MB gzipped; a 6,000-point agreement gate, measured 99.95% with zero overlaps; an exact 3,569 count, after the five areas of Lake Pontchartrain the file marks as in no voting district are left out). 7.8 MB, 2.31 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

Louisiana's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — four reservations and two pieces of off-reservation trust land, held by four nations. The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-10-20; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

rosters.note: U.S. House (LA) roster, refreshed weekly by update-la-congress-roster.yml.

Louisiana Senate roster from the Senate's own list of senators and their pages, one record per seat, refreshed weekly. A vacant seat carries a record saying so, so the floor is the chamber's size; Senate District 14 read vacant on 2026-10-20.
Louisiana House roster on the same terms; House Districts 77 and 92 read vacant on 2026-10-20.

Every parish's governing body by seat and its parish president or mayor, from the Secretary of State's list of elected officials, one record per parish, refreshed weekly by update-la-parish-officials.yml.

The mayor, council or board of aldermen and chief of police or marshal of every municipality the Secretary of State's list names, keyed by the Census place id, built from the same weekly read of the list by la/scripts/build_la_local_officials.py; 302 on 2026-10-20.
The members of all 69 school boards, keyed by the Census school district id, built in the same run; the builder refuses unless every district has a board.
The parishes whose districts the Police Jury or Council District layer draws, written by the same build as la-parish-districts.json; the layer's coverage test reads it.

The councils of the three Louisiana nations whose own pages name them (the Chitimacha, the Jena Band of Choctaw and the Tunica-Biloxi), keyed by the Census AIANNH code of their land — scripts/build_tribal_areas.py --rosters from data/tribal-councils.json, which scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py re-reads weekly (update-tribal-councils.yml, listed in the Wisconsin worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance). Merged onto tribal-areas.json by the layer's loader, so the land stays cache-first and the names network-first.
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.
